description:
## Summary

- Add a session name input field to GUI for multi-turn persistent conversations
- Enable GUI users to use the same session functionality as CLI `--session` flag
- Session data is persisted to `~/.config/fabric/sessions/`

## Changes

- **Backend**: Add `SessionName` field to `PromptRequest` and pass it to `domain.ChatRequest`
- **Frontend**: Add `sessionName` to `ChatPrompt` interface and include it in chat requests
- **UI**: Add Session Name input with dropdown for existing sessions in `DropdownGroup.svelte`

## Test plan

- [ ] Start backend with `fabric --serve`
- [ ] Start frontend with `cd web && npm run dev`
- [ ] Enter a session name in the "Session Name" field
- [ ] Send multiple messages and verify conversation context is preserved
- [ ] Verify session file is created in `~/.config/fabric/sessions/`
- [ ] Select an existing session from dropdown and continue the conversation.

Closes #680

comments.body: The dropdown doesn't have a `value` binding, so after a user selects a session, the dropdown will visually reset to the placeholder option "Load existing session..." even though the session has been set. Consider adding `bind:value={sessionInput}` or tracking the selected value separately to provide better visual feedback.

The comment refers to "Session ID" but the field is named "sessionName" throughout the codebase. Consider using "Session Name" in the label to match the actual field naming, or rename the field to "sessionId" if "Session ID" is the preferred term. Consistency in terminology helps reduce confusion.
```suggestion
      <Label for="session-input" class="text-xs text-white/70 mb-1 block">Session Name</Label>
```

The session management UI is embedded directly in DropdownGroup.svelte, which violates the single responsibility principle.

Looking at the codebase structure, there's already a dedicated `SessionManager.svelte` 

DropdownGroup.svelte now handles patterns, models, languages, strategies, sessions, AND pattern variables

Other components, like `Models.svelte` and `Patterns.svelte`, are dedicated to single concerns.

The component is becoming a "god component".

Recommendation: Extract the session input/selection UI into a separate `SessionSelector.svelte` component following the pattern of existing components:

This uses a native HTML < select > element instead of the `Select` component used throughout the rest of the file. Current:

```html
< select
  on:change={handleSessionSelect}
  class="w-full mt-2 px-3 py-2 text-sm bg-primary-800/30 border-none rounded-md hover:bg-primary-800/40 transition-colors text-white focus:ring-1 focus:ring-white/20 focus:outline-none"
>
```

Should be:

```html
<Select
  on:change={handleSessionSelect}
  class="mt-2 bg-primary-800/30 border-none hover:bg-primary-800/40 transition-colors"
>
```

Reactive statement is not necessary here. Could be simplified like this:

```javascript
$: sessionsList = $sessions?.map(s => s.Name) ?? [];
```

This is more concise and handles the null case explicitly.

You can replace this with this line instead:

```javascript
sessionName: get(currentSession) ?? undefined,
```
